/-!
# Conjecture 10.53

by S. V. Rychkov

(M. Dugas). Let $\mathfrak{R}$ be the *Reid class*, i.e. the smallest class of abelian
groups containing $\mathbb{Z}$ and closed under direct sums and direct products.
Is $\mathfrak{R}$ closed under direct summands?

Here "direct sums" are the (restricted) direct sums $\bigoplus_{i \in I} G_i$ and
"direct products" are the (unrestricted) direct products $\prod_{i \in I} G_i$ over
arbitrary index sets $I$. The Reid class is regarded as a class of abelian groups up to
isomorphism, so it is also closed under isomorphism. The problem was proposed in the
10th issue of the notebook (1986).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

inductive ReidClass : (G : Type) → [AddCommGroup G] → Prop
  /-- $\mathbb{Z} \in \mathfrak{R}$. -/
  | int : ReidClass ℤ
  /-- $\mathfrak{R}$ is closed under isomorphism. -/
  | of_addEquiv {G H : Type} [AddCommGroup G] [AddCommGroup H] :
      ReidClass G → (G ≃+ H) → ReidClass H
  /-- $\mathfrak{R}$ is closed under direct sums $\bigoplus_{i \in I} G_i$. -/
  | directSum {ι : Type} (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] :
      (∀ i, ReidClass (G i)) → ReidClass (⨁ i, G i)
  /-- $\mathfrak{R}$ is closed under direct products $\prod_{i \in I} G_i$. -/
  | pi {ι : Type} (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] :
      (∀ i, ReidClass (G i)) → ReidClass (∀ i, G i)

The *Reid class* $\mathfrak{R}$: the smallest class of abelian groups containing
$\mathbb{Z}$ and closed under isomorphism, arbitrary direct sums and arbitrary direct

type (so the trivial group belongs to $\mathfrak{R}$).

inductive ReidClass : (G : Type) → [AddCommGroup G] → Prop
  /-- $\mathbb{Z} \in \mathfrak{R}$. -/
  | int : ReidClass ℤ
  /-- $\mathfrak{R}$ is closed under isomorphism. -/
  | of_addEquiv {G H : Type} [AddCommGroup G] [AddCommGroup H] :
      ReidClass G → (G ≃+ H) → ReidClass H
  /-- $\mathfrak{R}$ is closed under direct sums $\bigoplus_{i \in I} G_i$. -/
  | directSum {ι : Type} (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] :
      (∀ i, ReidClass (G i)) → ReidClass (⨁ i, G i)
  /-- $\mathfrak{R}$ is closed under direct products $\prod_{i \in I} G_i$. -/
  | pi {ι : Type} (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] :
      (∀ i, ReidClass (G i)) → ReidClass (∀ i, G i)

(M. Dugas). Let $\mathfrak{R}$ be the *Reid class*, i.e. the smallest class of abelian

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no question: the implicit ambient category is abelian groups (the Reid class is the smallest class of abelian groups, closed under isomorphism, containing ℤ and closed under arbitrary — possibly infinite — direct sums and direct products), and the Prop asks whether every direct summand of a group in this class is again (isomorphic to a group) in the class; 'the smallest' elides the word 'class'.
claims.reviewer_why: c04's inductive predicate `ReidClass : (G : Type) → [AddCommGroup G] → Prop` (constructors: ℤ, closure under `≃+`, arbitrary `⨁ i, G i`, arbitrary `∀ i, G i`) is the least fixed point, i.e. exactly 'the smallest class of abelian groups containing ℤ, closed under isomorphism, direct sums and direct products' over arbitrary (incl. empty/infinite) index sets. The question is `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G, ReidClass G → ∀ A B : AddSubgroup G, IsCompl A B → ReidClass A`; I verified in a scratch file that `IsCompl A B` on additive subgroups of an abelian group yields `A × B ≃+ G`, so with iso-closure this is precisely 'every direct summand of a member is a member'. answer(True) = positive answer. Chosen over the near-identical c01/c05/c07 for the clearest docstrings (constructor docs, explicit empty-index convention, explanation of `IsCompl`), `category test` tags on the sanity lemmas, no extraneous `DecidableEq` hypothesis (c01), and adherence to the Kourovka `(G : Type) [..]` idiom. Family B (c02, c03, c06, c08: `AddCommGrpCat`, impredicative intersection / `≃+ H × K` / retract / split mono) are also mathematically faithful but add categorical machinery, three are universe-polymorphic (asserting a single answer for every universe) and none includes API tests for the bespoke definition. Shipped c04 verbatim; compiles with only the sorry warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.53

by S. V. Rychkov

(M. Dugas). Let $\mathfrak{R}$ be the *Reid class*, i.e. the smallest class of abelian
groups containing $\mathbb{Z}$ and closed under direct sums and direct products.
Is $\mathfrak{R}$ closed under direct summands?

Here "direct sums" are the (restricted) direct sums $\bigoplus_{i \in I} G_i$ and
"direct products" are the (unrestricted) direct products $\prod_{i \in I} G_i$ over
arbitrary index sets $I$. The Reid class is regarded as a class of abelian groups up to
isomorphism, so it is also closed under isomorphism. The problem was proposed in the
10th issue of the notebook (1986).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.53»

open DirectSum

/--
The *Reid class* $\mathfrak{R}$: the smallest class of abelian groups containing
$\mathbb{Z}$ and closed under isomorphism, arbitrary direct sums and arbitrary direct
products. `ReidClass G` means that the abelian group `G` belongs to $\mathfrak{R}$.

The index type of a direct sum or direct product may be any type, including the empty
type (so the trivial group belongs to $\mathfrak{R}$).
-/
inductive ReidClass : (G : Type) → [AddCommGroup G] → Prop
  /-- $\mathbb{Z} \in \mathfrak{R}$. -/
  | int : ReidClass ℤ
  /-- $\mathfrak{R}$ is closed under isomorphism. -/
  | of_addEquiv {G H : Type} [AddCommGroup G] [AddCommGroup H] :
      ReidClass G → (G ≃+ H) → ReidClass H
  /-- $\mathfrak{R}$ is closed under direct sums $\bigoplus_{i \in I} G_i$. -/
  | directSum {ι : Type} (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] :
      (∀ i, ReidClass (G i)) → ReidClass (⨁ i, G i)
  /-- $\mathfrak{R}$ is closed under direct products $\prod_{i \in I} G_i$. -/
  | pi {ι : Type} (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] :
      (∀ i, ReidClass (G i)) → ReidClass (∀ i, G i)

/-- The trivial group belongs to the Reid class (as the empty direct product). -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem reidClass_punit : ReidClass PUnit :=
  (ReidClass.pi (ι := Empty) (fun _ => ℤ) fun i => i.elim).of_addEquiv AddEquiv.ofUnique

/-- The free abelian group of countable rank $\mathbb{Z}^{(\omega)}$ belongs to the
Reid class. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem reidClass_directSum_nat_int : ReidClass (⨁ _ : ℕ, ℤ) :=
  ReidClass.directSum (fun _ => ℤ) fun _ => ReidClass.int

/-- The Baer–Specker group $\mathbb{Z}^{\omega}$ belongs to the Reid class. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem reidClass_pi_nat_int : ReidClass (ℕ → ℤ) :=
  ReidClass.pi (fun _ => ℤ) fun _ => ReidClass.int

/--
(M. Dugas). Let $\mathfrak{R}$ be the *Reid class*, i.e. the smallest class of abelian
groups containing $\mathbb{Z}$ and closed under direct sums and direct products.
Is $\mathfrak{R}$ closed under direct summands?

That is: if $G \in \mathfrak{R}$ and $G = A \oplus B$ for subgroups $A, B \leq G$
(formalised as `IsCompl A B` in the lattice of subgroups of $G$), is $A \in \mathfrak{R}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.53» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [AddCommGroup G], ReidClass G →
      ∀ A B : AddSubgroup G, IsCompl A B → ReidClass A := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.53»

items: Ambient category is abelian groups (`AddCommGroup`), as the decomposition table specifies; the class is a predicate on types `G : Type` with `[AddCommGroup G]`, following the `(G : Type) [Group G]` idiom of the other Kourovka files (universe fixed to `Type`, index types also in `Type`; Type is closed under the constructions so the class is self-contained).

The Reid class is defined as an inductive predicate (least fixed point), which is the standard Lean idiom for 'the smallest class containing ... and closed under ...'. Closure under isomorphism (`G ≃+ H`) is built in as a constructor, as the table's notes require; without it the question would be trivially negative (even `⊤ : AddSubgroup ℤ` is only isomorphic to ℤ).

Direct sums are the restricted direct sums `DirectSum ι G` (`⨁ i, G i`) and direct products are the unrestricted products `∀ i, G i`, over arbitrary index types `ι : Type` (possibly infinite, possibly empty). Allowing the empty index type puts the trivial group in the class; excluding it would make the question vacuously 'no' (the zero group is a direct summand of ℤ) and does not otherwise change the class up to isomorphism, so this is the intended reading.

'Direct summand' is formalised internally: `A` is a summand of `G` iff there is `B : AddSubgroup G` with `IsCompl A B` (i.e. `A ⊓ B = ⊥ ∧ A ⊔ B = ⊤`, hence `G = A ⊕ B`). With iso-closure this is equivalent to the external formulation `ReidClass (A × B) → ReidClass A`.
Three `@[category test]` statements with one-line proofs sanity-check the definition (trivial group, ℤ^(ω), Baer–Specker group ℤ^ω); the trivial-group test documents the empty-index convention.

reviewer_notes: Original statement elides 'class of abelian groups'; all candidates and the decomposition agree the ambient category is abelian groups (Reid's class, cf. Fuchs / Dugas–Zimmermann-Huisgen), and that the class is isomorphism-closed (otherwise the question is meaningless for concrete types). Direct sums = restricted direct sums (`DirectSum`), direct products = full Pi types, both over arbitrary index types in `Type`; the empty index gives the trivial group, which must be in the class anyway (it is a summand of ℤ). Universe fixed to `Type` as in the other Kourovka files; `Type` is closed under all the constructions, so nothing relevant escapes it. No candidate omitted the slot and none raised decomposition objections; all eight compiled. Internal (`IsCompl`) vs external (`G ≃+ H × K`) summand formulations are equivalent given iso-closure; the shipped file documents the internal one in the theorem docstring.
